title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Solenoid "B" High
plain: The wastegate solenoid helps control how much boost the turbo makes. Its control circuit reads higher than expected, often from a short to power or an open.
symptoms: Boost may surge or feel too strong at times
checks: Inspect the solenoid connector, wiring and vacuum hoses
Check the solenoid's resistance and command it with a scan tool
fix: Usually a new wastegate control solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control "A" (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
plain: On diesel engines, this system controls how much fuel the injection pump delivers. The computer sees a problem in this control circuit.

causes.name: Faulty fuel metering solenoid or injection pump electronics
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the pump
Low fuel supply from a clogged filter, weak lift pump or air in the fuel

checks: Check fuel supply pressure and replace a dirty fuel filter
Inspect the injection pump connector and wiring
Check the control circuit's resistance and voltage with a meter
fix: Often a fuel supply repair or a new injection pump. Confirm fuel supply is good before replacing the pump.
examples: Well known on Dodge Ram Cummins diesels with the VP44 injection pump

title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control "A" Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
plain: On diesel engines, this system controls how much fuel the injection pump delivers. The amount of fuel being delivered doesn't match what the computer is asking for.

causes.name: Faulty fuel metering solenoid or injection pump electronics
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the pump
Low fuel supply from a clogged filter, weak lift pump or air in the fuel

checks: Check fuel supply pressure and replace a dirty fuel filter
Inspect the injection pump connector and wiring
Watch commanded versus actual fuel quantity on a scan tool
fix: Often a fuel supply repair or a new injection pump. Confirm fuel supply is good before replacing the pump.

title: Fuel Pump Module Control Circuit/Open
plain: Many newer vehicles run the fuel pump through a separate fuel pump control module, which takes orders from the engine computer. The computer sees an open (broken) circuit in that command line.
symptoms: Engine may crank but not start

causes.name: Damaged wiring or corroded connector between the engine computer and pump module
Faulty fuel pump control module (often from corrosion)

checks: Inspect the fuel pump module and its connectors for corrosion
Check the module's power, ground and command signal with a meter
Listen for the fuel pump to run when the key is turned on
fix: Usually a new fuel pump control module or a wiring or connector repair.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower-than-expected voltage in the cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit. This usually points to a short to ground or a bad injector.
symptoms: Misfire, often with a cylinder 1 misfire code
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Shorted coil in the cylinder 1 injector
Faulty injector driver in the engine computer

checks: Measure the injector's resistance and compare it with the other injectors
Inspect the injector wiring for rubbing or melted insulation
fix: Usually a new injector or a wiring repair.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher-than-expected voltage in the cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit. This usually points to an unplugged or broken circuit, or a wire shorted to power.
symptoms: Misfire, often with a cylinder 1 misfire code
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Open coil in the cylinder 1 injector
Faulty injector driver in the engine computer

checks: Make sure the injector connector is fully plugged in and its pins are clean
Measure the injector's resistance and check the wiring for breaks
fix: Usually reconnecting or repairing the injector wiring, or a new injector.

title: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance
plain: The computer compares how much each cylinder helps spin the engine. Cylinder 1 is doing noticeably more or less work than the others.
symptoms: Extra smoke from the exhaust on diesels

causes.name: Weak, leaking or clogged injector on cylinder 1
Ignition problem on that cylinder (gas engines)

checks: Run a cylinder balance or contribution test with a scan tool
Do a compression test on that cylinder
Inspect the injector connector and wiring
fix: Most often a new injector for that cylinder. A compression problem means deeper engine repair.
